name: Pulsating red giant (Gaia DR3 2160548942811758720)
tagline: A giant star that swells and fades
blurb: A long-period variable (Gaia: ~372-day period) next to the north ecliptic pole, where SPHEREx looks every day. Frames here are two-month bins of 480 exposures sampled from 17,000.
notes: Its centre saturates in every detector; the light curve uses a ring around the centre instead.

cube.note: SPHEREx all-sky spectral map: each channel is the average of every visit up to the release, so different channels at one spot come from different dates.

finecube.note: Built from the single SPHEREx exposures at 6.15" pixels: each channel averages every exposure whose wavelength at that spot falls in it, over all visits, so different channels come from different dates.

flags.meaning: percent of the visit's exposures on that detector flagged at the pixel (255 = not covered)

colour_hint: This giant is blown out (white) at most wavelengths, and because it pulses, the map (an average over a year) mixes its bright and faint moments. Its story is in Blink and its light curve.

provenance.label: IRSA DR1+QR3 (baked 2026-11-15)
